unit_materialization_rule: Each row is one parse unit. locators enumerates all same-path/same-standing source distinctions retained inside that unit; mixed standings are separate rows.

units.normalized_content: ARC is a research framework for governed self-modification; RAHU is described as its adversarial benchmark; the repository tree shown in README is explicitly planned rather than a guarantee of current implementation.

ARC asks whether systems can repair invalidated structure without destroying retained structure; hypothesizes heterogeneous plasticity and diagnostic control; proposes C_future(t+1)>=C_future(t); predicts advantage from localization/controlled modification under deep shocks and a crossover near AAR*≈1.
Control pipeline is Error→Diagnosis→Permission→Allocation→Correction and Gamma→P(L_i|E_t)→FA_c→lambda_A→Pi_A→DeltaS→RI→C_future; FA_c<tau_c is specified to drive lambda_A toward zero.

Defines Gamma as reality coupling, P(L_i|E_t) as failure attribution, candidate failure depths, FA_c as attribution confidence, lambda_A as permission, Pi_A as plasticity allocation, RI as recovery intelligence, and C_future as future adaptive capacity.

Specifies four RAHU shock classes, comparison agents Flat/Meta/ARC-Lite/ARC-Full/Oracle Reset, candidate metrics AE_w/retention/RI/C_future, falsification criteria, and a future empirical-validation sequence.
Current status is research prototype phase; empirical validation is described as the next phase.
README does not establish empirical estimators for AAR components, causal identification of C_future, a calibration procedure for FA_c, or an observed AAR*≈1 boundary.
The charter is a research-design and falsification document and explicitly states that its purpose is not to argue that ARC works.

Charter hypothesizes advantage from governing permission/location/magnitude under heterogeneous failure depth/cost; requires external-evidence coupling; proposes lowest-sufficient-layer modification and non-decreasing future capacity; predicts different regimes below/above AAR*=1 and frames localization/future-capacity questions conditionally.

Defines RI_ARC>RI_baseline when AAR*>1; AAR*=Expected Blast Radius Prevented/(Diagnostic Cost+Intervention Risk); proposes FA_c as a calibration function; constrains lambda_A to [0,1], FA_c<tau_c→lambda_A→0, and sum Pi_A=1.
Defines structural hierarchy L0 parameter through L4 ontology; T_H holding duration; attribution, permission, allocation and future-capacity invariant failure classes.

Specifies oracle/learned/baseline comparisons and falsification; candidate future-shock and reachable-space measurements; bounded exploration after prolonged holding; ambiguity/cost/governor/attribution attacks; a minimum hierarchy including world-model failure and five shocks; explicit scientific support/rejection conditions.
Governor reliability is itself an explicit research problem, with false freezes, unnecessary deep rewrites, delayed recovery and confidence miscalibration named as failure signals.
Empirical estimators for AAR components, FA_c calibration/counterfactual consistency, C_future construct identification, T_max, lambda_A*, and governor reliability C_G are not specified.
